**Randersklyngen** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in Denmark [^src6]. It is one of the regional units monitored in the national quality assurance programs for cardiovascular care, specifically regarding the treatment and management of [[atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation) [^src1].

In the evaluation of clinical quality indicators, Randersklyngen has demonstrated strong performance in initiating anticoagulation therapy. For Indikator 1, which measures the timely start of treatment for newly diagnosed patients, the cluster achieved a result of 93.5%, successfully fulfilling the national standard [^src1]. This high level of compliance is also reflected in longer-term treatment coverage metrics, such as 1-year and 2-year anticoagulation coverage (Indikator 4a1 and 4a2), where the cluster maintains high percentages of treated patients [^src2]. 

Despite these successes in pharmacological treatment, the cluster faces challenges in non-pharmacological interventions. For [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed patients receiving structured patient education within their first year, Randersklyngen scored 42% [^src5]. While this falls short of the national standard, it is noted as being quite close to fulfilling the requirement, mirroring broader systemic barriers in implementing structured education across Danish healthcare clusters [^src5].

Furthermore, Randersklyngen's patient outcomes are closely monitored for adverse events. The cluster's data contributes to national mapping of the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) among atrial fibrillation patients [^src4]. Additional tracking includes the rates of severe bleeding within one year of diagnosis (Indikator 11) and the development of heart failure (Indikator 15), allowing for regional benchmarking against other clusters like [[midtklyngen|Midtklyngen]], [[horsensklyngen|Horsensklyngen]], and [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]] [^src7] [^src8].
